layout_dets.text: Improvements in corrosion resistance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Improvements in corrosion resistance, mechanical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: properties, and weldability of duplex

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: austenitic/ferritic steels*

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Verbesserung der Korrosionsbeständigkeit, der mechanischen Eigenschaften und der

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Schweißbarkeit von austenitisch-ferritischen Stählen

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: C. A. Clark and P. Guha**

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The corrosion behaviour, toughness and weldability of duplex

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stainless steel can be improved by controlling the composition and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: austenite: ferrite ratio in the base metal and in the weld deposits.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Addition of nitrogen is beneficial to ductility and restistance to pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion; the latter is also improved by increased chromium contents

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which stabilize the passive film. This effect is further enhanced by the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: addition of molybdenum which, however, should not exceed sigma

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: phase at high temperatures. Copper in amounts up to 1.5% improves

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the resistance to marine environments; however, a certain upper limit

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: should not be exceeded because of adverse effects on hot ductility. In

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: view of the function of nickel concerning the austenite : ferrite ratio

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (which should be about 50: 50) the nickel content should be appropri-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ately selected and should be higher in the filter metal.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: When considering materials for the construction of chemical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plant and for applications in marine environments, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: austenitic stainless steels have limitations associated with their

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: low strength, and, under appropriate conditions, susceptibility

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to stress corrosion, pitting corrosion, and crevice corrosion.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The higher alloyed fully austenitic steels, with nickel contents

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in excess of 25%, which may be specified for the more corro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sive acid environments such as sulphuric and phosphoric acids

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and sour oil well conditions, also present welding problems

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: due to lack of hot strength leading to fissuring in the weld

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: metal [1]. Changes in the design of chemical plant to give

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: higher yields often involve higher service temperatures and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: more concentrated and corrosive media, with a corresponding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: need for improved materials. The duplex austenitic-ferritic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels of high chromium content were therefore developed in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an attempt to combine the advantages of both the austenite

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Korrosionsverhalten, Festigkeit und Schweißbarkeit von nichtro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stenden Stählen mit Duplex-Gefüge können durch entsprechende

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Zusammensetzung und Einstellung des Austenit : Ferrit-Verhältnisses

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: im Grundwerkstoff und im Schweißgut verbessert werden. Zusatz von

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Stickstoff verbessert die Duktilität und die Lochkorrosionsbeständig-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: keit; diese wird ebenfalls verbessert durch erhöhte Chromgehalte,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: welche die Passivierungsschicht stabilisieren. Diese Wirkung wird

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: noch verstärkt durch Zusatz von Molybdän, das jedoch bestimmte

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Grenzen nicht überschreiten darf, da sonst die Gefahr der Sigma-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Phasen-Sprödigkeit bei höheren Temperaturen besteht. Auch Kupfer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in Mengen bis 1,5% verbessert die Korrosionsbeständigkeit besonders

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in Meerwasser, doch sollte wegen der abträglichen Wirkung auf die

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Warmzähigkeit ein bestimmter Gehalt nicht überschritten werden.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Wegen der wichtigen Rolle von Nickel für das Austenit : Ferrit-Ver-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hältnis (vorzugsweise 50: 50) muß der Nickelgehalt entsprechend

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gewählt werden und sollte im Schweißgut etwas erhöht werden.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and ferrite phases, the austenite imparting toughness and gen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: eral corrosion resistance, and the ferrite imparting strength

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and resistance to stress corrosion cracking. These were first

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: introduced for castings in the mid-1930's but did not initially

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gain much favour, as the microstructure was not adequately

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: controlled, resulting in embrittlement and failure to achieve

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the potential corrosion resisting capabilities. Wrought duplex

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels, containing about 1.5% molybdenum, were introduced

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in Germany in the late 1920's [2], but were only regarded as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: having corrosion resistance equivalent to the 316-type steels,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: their main attribute being much increased strength. The major

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: advance was achieved by the addition of copper to give the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cast alloy CD 4MCu [3] developed by the Alloy Casting Insti-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tute of America.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: However, this alloy can suffer from lack of toughness which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can lead to problems during welding and difficulties in avoid-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing fettling cracks and quench cracks when cutting and heat

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: treating castings of heavy section.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This paper indicates how variations in composition affect

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the properties of duplex steels and gives the characteristics of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: two such steels, developed subsequent to CD 4 MCu, whose

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compositions have been balanced to optimise microstructure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and provide attractive combinations of corrosion characteris-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tics, mechanical properties, and ease of production.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Variations in composition and microstructure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a) Nitrogen

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The most significant improvement in both corrosion charac-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: teristcs and mechanical properties, compared with nitrogen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: free duplex steels is obtained by the addition of nitrogen in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: excess of 0.1%. Studies on castings of large section, indicated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that addition of nitrogen increases the pitting potential in 3%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: NaCl solution at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from 0.45 V (S.H.E.) to 1.15 V

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (S.H.E.) for steels containing approximately 25% Cr, 5% Ni,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.4% Mo, and 3% Cu. When steels of this composition in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: form of thick sections (76 mm) were solution treated and then

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aged it was found that the nitrogen-free steel was brittle, giv-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing zero elongation during tensile testing, whilst the nitrogen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: containing steel gave an elongation above 20% [4].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In CD 4 MCu, where nitrogen is not added, it is necessary to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: limit the carbon content to a maximum of 0.04% in order to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: avoid intercrystalline corrosion and weld decay in nitric acid

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tests [5], whereas a maximum of 0.08% carbon can be permit-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ted in steels of similar composition to which nitrogen has been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: added, thus reducing composition control problems during

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: selection of raw materials, melting operations, and recycling of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: remelt. Further beneficial effects of nitrogen, on the pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance of steels of carbon content greater than 0.04% are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: illustrated in Figure 1.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 1. The effect of nitrogen additions on the pitting potentials in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3% NaCl at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 0.07% carbon

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abb. 1. Einfluß von Stickstoff-Zusätzen auf die Lochkorrosionspo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tentiale in 3%iger NaCl-Lösung von

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: für austenitisch-ferritische

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Stähle mit etwa 0,04 und 0,07% Kohlenstoff

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The nitrogen addition reinforces nickel in acting as an auste-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nite stabiliser, but also appears to modify the austenite-ferrite

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ratio at which maximum pitting resistance is achieved. For

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: example the CD4MCu composition appears to have been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: optimised to give an austenite-ferrite ratio of 25-27 [3],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: whereas similar steels containing about 0.15% nitrogen give

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: maximum resistance to pitting with an austenite-ferrite ratio of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: about 50–50.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: b) Nickel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: With other elements constant, it is found that the optimum

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting resistance is achieved by selecting a nickel content to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: give an austenite-ferrite ratio of about 50%. In a steel contain-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3% Cu, 2.5% Mo, and 0.15% N for example, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: maximum pitting potential in 3% NaCl at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is achieved

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: when the nickel content is about 5.2%. The pitting potentials

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in 3% NaCl at 30°C for steels of varying nickel contents are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: illustrated in Fig. 2. For a steel of composition 28% Cr, 1.5%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Cu, 2.5% Mo and 0.15% N, the optimum nickel content for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: maximum resistance to pitting combined with good toughness

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is about 8%.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It is therefore considered that the main role of nickel is to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: control the microstructure, rather than to modify the corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance per se. If nickel contents are significantly in excess

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the optimum, so that the austenite content increases above

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 50% the residual ferrite becomes increasingly enriched in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chromium, a ferrite stabiliser. This high-chromium ferrite

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: more readily transforms to brittle sigma phase at temperatures

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the range

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with adverse effects on hot working

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: characteristics for wrought steels, impact toughness of cast

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels, and weldability.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Conversely, if the nickel content is reduced below the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: optimum, leading to high ferrite contents, low toughness will

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: again result because the delta ferrite formed immediately on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solidification also tends to have low ductility. As indicated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: later, this effect is also significant when considering the welda-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bility of duplex steels.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: c) Chromium and molybdenum

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Both chromium and molybdenum are beneficial in increas-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing the pitting resistance of stainless steels generally. Thus, for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a duplex steel containing 5% Ni, 3% Cu, 2.5% Mo, and 0.15%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: N, increase in chromium from 22.5% to 28% decreased the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting current density monotonically in 3% NaCl solution at

layout_dets.text: Improvements in corrosion resistance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: As reported by Oldfield and Sutton [6] and by Brigham [7]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: both chromium and molybdenum also improve resistance to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crevice corrosion. Molybdenum is regarded as more effective

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: than chromium, but in practice it is desirable to limit the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: molybdenum content because it strongly promotes the forma-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion of sigma phase [8]. This may lead to adverse effects on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: properties following welding or processing of steels in the tem-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: perature range

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In practice therefore it has been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: found convenient to hold the molybdenum content within the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: range 2–3%, improve passivation characteristics by increasing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chromium, and control the austenite-ferrite ratio by corres-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ponding adjustments to the nickel content.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: d) Copper

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It has been shown that additions of copper to a duplex steel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in amounts up to about 1.0% are beneficial in increasing the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting resistance in 3% NaCl solution, but that higher copper

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contents give little further improvement [9]. However higher

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: copper contents are beneficial in lower pH environments that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are experienced in sour oil wells, polluted sea water, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chemical process plant, particularly under conditions of high

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: flow velocity leading to erosion and cavitation, although under

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: very severe conditions of this kind, the more expensive super

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: austenite steels or high nickel alloys might be required. High

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: copper contents, however, tend to reduce hot ductility and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: weldability so that for wrought duplex steels copper is usually

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: limited to a maximum of about 2% and for the cast steels to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: about 3%. Copper is a weak austenite stabiliser and therefore

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: slightly reinforces the effects of nickel and nitrogen on micro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structure.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The general effects of the variations in composition,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: described above, on corrosion resistance and mechanical prop-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: erties are illustrated in Fig. 2 and 3 and Table 1 respectively. It

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is seen that the impact toughness for material in the aged

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: condition is particularly sensitive to deviation from the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: optimum composition.

layout_dets.text: Resulting from these properties, FERRALIUM alloy 255 is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: certain critical conditions in the wet process for the production

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Improvements in corrosion resistance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steel is worked, the austenite phase, being ductile, becomes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: elongated along the direction of deformation. It has been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shown that because of their very high cooling rate, weld metal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: deposits produced from matching filler rods by the manual

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: metal arc technique, contain a somewhat higher ferrite content

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and also have a more acicular microstructure than the parent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: metal [11]. Because delta ferrite tends to have low ductility the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: net effect of these microstructural differences is to impart

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lower toughness to weld metal compared with parent material

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the same composition. This low toughness can lead to crack-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing in the weld metal when producing thick section welds

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: under severe restraint. The problem was overcome by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: developing electrodes of higher nickel content (6.9%) so as to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: produce weld deposits of higher austenite content than the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parent metal, FERRALIUM 255. Although the microstruc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ture was still very acicular the ductility was satisfactorily

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: restored as shown in Table 4. Measurements of pitting poten-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tials in 3% NaCl solution indicated that weld deposits from the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: higher nickel electrodes had similar characteristics to those of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the parent metal.

layout_dets.text: Conclusions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. The addition of nitrogen to duplex steels is beneficial to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: both ductility and resistance to pitting corrosion. The max-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: imum permitted carbon content can also be raised from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 0.04 to 0.08%, when nitrogen is added, without adversely

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: affecting resistance to pitting and intercrystalline corrosion.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. The most important function of nickel in duplex steels is to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: balance the austenite-ferrite microstructure and it is consid-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ered that a 50–50 ratio gives optimum properties.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. Pitting current density measurements in 3% NaCl at 30°C

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with varying chromium contents indicate that increasing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chromium content improves the stability of the passive film.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4. Molybdenum reinforces the beneficial effects of chromium

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: but has to be limited because of cost and its tendency to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: promote the formation of brittle sigma phase at high tem-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: peratures.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5. Copper in amounts up to 1.5% improves pitting resistance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in marine environments, and higher levels are beneficial in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: low pH solutions. The practical upper limits for copper in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: duplex steel castings and wrought products are restricted by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adverse effects on hot ductility.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 6. Because of the high quench rates during welding opera-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions, weld deposits from electrodes of matching composi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion tend to have higher ferrite contents, more acicular mic-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rostructures, and lower ductilities than the parent metal.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Welding consumables for duplex steels should therefore

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: preferably contain higher nickel contents than the parent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: metal.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 7. Two commercial duplex steels, FERRALIUM alloy 255

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (25 Cr, 5Ni, Mo, Cu, N) and FERRALIUM alloy 288,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (28 Cr, 8 Ni, Mo, Cu, N) together with compatible welding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: electrodes, have been developed using the principles out-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lined above. The former steel, in both cast and wrought

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: forms, has found wide application in marine environments

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and chemical process plant. The latter steel, in the form of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: castings, is finding increasing application in more critical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: applications, including the production of “wet" process

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: phosphoric acid.
